name: Toy ruleset
description: The fast unit-test ruleset. Its constants are the original's confirmed values, transcribed from the reports in the research repository's docs/reports/ and cited per field in the sibling "_provenance" blocks; its flags are set the way the shipped classical-faithful preset sets them. It exists so tests do not depend on the full classical-mediterranean world, which task T29 exports separately.

_provenance.weekStep: confirmed: decompiled-turn-and-calendar-sequencing.md — the week advances by +2 each turn cycle.
_provenance.seasonAdvanceFromWeek: confirmed: decompiled-turn-and-calendar-sequencing.md — the season advances at the 11 to 1 wrap.
_provenance.seasonsPerYear: confirmed: decompiled-quarterly-billing-and-economy.md — 'quarterly' is once per season, four times a year; the year decrements at the Winter to Spring wrap.
_provenance.startWeek: confirmed: impconq2-full-save-analysis.md and one-turn-save-comparison.md — the earliest news slot in the sample saves reads 'Week 1      Spring      270 BC', and the next turn's slot reads 'Week  3      Spring      270BC'. The parity is load-bearing rather than cosmetic: decompiled-turn-and-calendar-sequencing.md gives the cycle as 'week = (week + 2) mod 12; if week == 1: season++', so only an odd start ever reaches the season boundary. Every dated save in the project (weeks 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 — saves-and-screenshots.md, strategic-recording-and-summer-saves.md) is on that odd parity.
_provenance.startSeasonIndex: confirmed: saves-and-screenshots.md and strategic-recording-and-summer-saves.md — the save trailer's +44 byte is 0 in all five Spring saves and 1 in all three Summer saves, so season index 0 is Spring; impconq2-full-save-analysis.md shows the campaign's first dated news slot as Spring 270 BC.
_provenance.startYearBc: confirmed: decompiled-diplomacy-peace-terms-and-instant-battles.md — THumanFalls_InitializeForm reports the reign length as 270 minus the current year, confirming the 270 BC start.
_provenance.cityUnitStateCodeStep: confirmed: decompiled-turn-and-calendar-sequencing.md — city-unit StateCode increments by 2 per week.
_provenance.cityUnitStateCodeCap: confirmed: decompiled-turn-and-calendar-sequencing.md — capped at 24 (a cap, not a starting value).

_provenance.recruitCost: confirmed: unit-type-stat-table-in-dat.md — +0x22, the initial recruit cost.
_provenance.quarterlyPrice: confirmed: unit-type-stat-table-in-dat.md — +0x24, the quarterly price used by upkeep and mercenary hire.
_provenance.combatPowerWeight: confirmed: decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md — +0x26, identified there as the per-type combat-power weight used by field-battle strength.

_provenance.shots: confirmed: unit-type-stat-table-in-dat.md — matches the '1st Lancers Battalion ... 9 shots' screenshot in battle-observation.md.
_provenance.recruitCost: confirmed: unit-type-stat-table-in-dat.md — independently solved from two save-diffs in decompiled-recruitment-cost-formula.md before the table was found.

_provenance.moveCosts: confirmed: terrain-move-cost-table-in-dat.md — the original's twelve-entry terrain table at DAT offset 0x1F622, verbatim: Sea 1, Sea 3, Plain 1, Desert 1, Forest 2, Mountains 4, and six River codes at 4. The table is keyed by tile-type id rather than by cell code so that a world with different or additional terrain types can be priced by the same ruleset shape; the twelve entries are shipped values, not a fixed size.
_provenance.defaultMoveCost: designed: docs/game-design.md §Movement — 'A custom World's new terrain types default to cost 1 unless a ruleset explicitly prices them'. Searched docs/reports/ for any original handling of an unpriced terrain code and found none to transcribe: terrain-move-cost-table-in-dat.md establishes that the original's table covers exactly codes 0-11 and that codes 12 and above are city/army/fleet markers rather than terrain, so the original has no unpriced-terrain case to copy.

_provenance.consumptionBaseValue: confirmed: investigations/thracia-supply-morale.md, citing decompiled-turn-and-calendar-sequencing.md's FUN_004514ec — per-turn consumption = ((90 - seasonVal) * troops) / 20000, decompiled directly and verified turn-for-turn against the Thracian army's spring consumption (142 -> 98 -> 54 -> 10, exactly -44 each turn).
_provenance.consumptionDivisor: confirmed: investigations/thracia-supply-morale.md — the 20000 divisor of the same expression.
_provenance.fleetEmbarkedDivisor: confirmed: investigations/thracia-supply-morale.md — an army aboard a fleet (army[+8] == -1) instead consumes max(0, supplies - troops/200), no seasonal term.
_provenance.seasonValues: confirmed: investigations/thracia-supply-morale.md — the season record at DAT offset 0x1F7D8, matching &DAT_004794a8 + season*10: Spring 50, Summer 80, Autumn 80, Winter 20, indexed by calendar.startSeasonIndex's convention (0=Spring). Winter costs 7x Summer, verified against the same investigation's seasonal-consumption table for a 22,000-troop army (44/11/11/77 tons).

_provenance.decayThresholdPercent: confirmed: investigations/thracia-supply-morale.md, FUN_004514ec — pct < 10 decays morale by 2 and costs one move; verified turn-for-turn against the Thracian army's 13-save series (12 of 12 transitions predicted exactly).
_provenance.deadBandUpperPercent: confirmed: investigations/thracia-supply-morale.md — 10 <= pct <= 15 is a deliberate dead band, no change.
_provenance.moraleFloor: confirmed: investigations/thracia-supply-morale.md — the real bound of the field: the army panel prints morale as a tier via moraleNames[(v-51)>>2], 51...70 being exactly five 4-wide tiers.
_provenance.regenAmount: confirmed: investigations/thracia-supply-morale.md — army[+14] += 1 when pct > 15, the confirmed 2:1 decay/regen asymmetry (decay is twice as fast as regen).
_provenance.moraleCeiling: confirmed: investigations/thracia-supply-morale.md — the real ceiling of the field.
_provenance.movesPenaltyOnDecay: confirmed: investigations/thracia-supply-morale.md — army[+6] -= 1 on the same pct < 10 branch that decays morale; verified against the Thracian series' moves column (9 while supplied, 8 from the first pct < 10 turn on).
_provenance.baseMovesMax: confirmed: investigations/thracia-supply-morale.md, FUN_004514ec — moves = 10 - min(5, troops / 20000), recomputed every turn before the decay penalty, not accumulated from the previous turn.
_provenance.movesTroopDivisor: confirmed: investigations/thracia-supply-morale.md — the troop divisor of the same base-moves expression; numerically the same 20000 as supplyConsumption.consumptionDivisor in the source pseudocode, kept as a separate field since the two formulas are conceptually distinct.
_provenance.movesReductionCap: confirmed: investigations/thracia-supply-morale.md — the min(5, ...) cap of the same expression.

effects.description: A storm damages a fleet at sea.

_provenance._group: designed: docs/game-design.md §Economy — 'implement as a data-driven table of possible weather effects (storm damages a fleet, drought reduces a region's supply, etc.) with the confirmed frequency curve and [designed] specific effects'. decompiled-weather-events.md confirms the frequency curve only; FUN_004511bc (the effect itself) was never decompiled, so no magnitude is transcribed here — this entry names the effect kind design-audit.md already suggests, nothing more.

effects.description: A drought reduces a region's supply.

_provenance._group: designed: docs/game-design.md §Economy, same open item as storm-damages-fleet — no magnitude transcribed, effect internals unrecovered.

_provenance.earlyLateWeekThreshold: confirmed: decompiled-weather-events.md — Spring's 'early'/'late' boundary is week < 6; Autumn's is week < 7 (the report gives the two seasons different boundaries, not the same one). Represented here as a single field because on this engine's odd-week calendar (weeks 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11) the two readings pick out exactly the same set of weeks either way, so a single shared threshold of 6 is behaviourally equivalent to carrying 6 and 7 separately (review round 1, B5). Summer and Winter are flat for the whole season, so their early/late split never matters.
_provenance.bySeason: confirmed: decompiled-weather-events.md — Spring early 1-in-15 / late 1-in-30; Summer 1-in-40; Autumn early 1-in-30 / late 1-in-15; Winter 1-in-5. Winter is roughly 8x more frequent than Summer (1/5 vs 1/40), the source for T08's DoD 8 ratio-band assertion, itself approximate per that report.
_provenance.locationCount: confirmed: decompiled-weather-events.md, DAT_00479540 — the frequency curve above is rolled independently once per tracked location, every tick, not once per tick overall (review round 1, B4). The locations' own identity is [open], exactly as the report leaves it; only the roll count is transcribed here.
_provenance.effects: designed: docs/game-design.md §Economy — the frequency curve is confirmed but the effects were never decompiled (FUN_004511bc, [open] per docs/design-audit.md §2.13); this table exists so an effect can be added as data later without an engine change, not because these two entries' specifics are evidenced.

_provenance.shipUpkeepPerQuarter: confirmed: fleet-order-at-caere.md and decompiled-fleet-tax-and-mercenary-formulas.md — ships cost 3 talents each per quarter.
_provenance.mobilizationDecayPerQuarter: confirmed: city-population-growth.md — renamed from unityDecayPerQuarter (bug #68): FUN_00451b40's nation-loop '-3' is applied to mobilization (+0x442), not unity; 71 of 80 nation-quarters matched exactly across 5 quarter pairs, the other 9 being AIs recruiting or disbanding in the round. decompiled-quarterly-billing-and-economy.md's original 'unity decays 3 per quarter, clamped at 0' misattributed the field.
_provenance.unityCap: confirmed: decompiled-diplomacy-peace-terms-and-instant-battles.md — the instant resolver clamps the winner's unity with min(990, ...); city-population-growth.md's own quarterly unity update (T35) clamps to this same cap.
_provenance.purseCapPerUnit: confirmed: decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md — TAFSupply_ChangeMoney caps an army's or fleet's own purse at 1,000 talents.
_provenance.supplyTonsPerTalent: confirmed: decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md — TAFSupply_TransferSupply charges amount / 5, i.e. 1 talent per 5 tons, from the buyer's purse to the selling city's owner. docs/design-audit.md Q9 is now answered by the user's own play experience: resupplying at a city the buying army's nation owns is free (no talent debit at all, matching the Galatia frames' unchanged army money and treasury); this amount/5 constant applies only to the paid, foreign-city case. Where a foreign purchase's talents end up is resolved by T38 (docs/task-catalogue.md Done-when 5, Q9's 2026-09-14 update): the selling city's owner's treasury, credited amount/5 by SupplyPurchase.BuyForArmy/BuyForFleet. Review round 1, N5: this text previously called the credit destination 'still [open]', which was already stale by the time this same PR closed it; corrected here rather than left contradicting the diff it belongs to.
_provenance.armySupplyTonsPerTroops: confirmed: decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md — army supply capacity is troops / 100 tons, reproducing all four recorded percentage readings.
_provenance.fleetSupplyTonsPerShip: confirmed: decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md — fleet supply capacity is ships × 8 tons; supply-capacity-rounding.md's instruction-level check confirms this same formula, with no +1, caps the supply dialog's fleet transfer on both the own-city (free) and foreign-city (paid) paths alike.
_provenance.supplyDialogArmyCapacityBonus: confirmed: supply-capacity-rounding.md — review round 3's resolution of round 2's R1. TAFSupply_ChangeSupply (own-city, free) and TAFSupply_ChangeBuyAmount (foreign, paid) both compute room as troops IDIV 100 then an unconditional INC, i.e. troops/100 + 1, with no FPU instruction and no Round/Trunc, applied identically on both paths. This is the supply *dialog's* cap only: armySupplyTonsPerTroops (troops/100, no +1) stays the general capacity every other path (automatic resupply, army-to-army rebalancing, battle absorption) uses, confirmed against 75 distinct army states in the saves; the dialog's own +1 is confirmed by exactly one state, the Roman 13-unit roster's 48,173-troop army going from 403 to 482 tons at Rome (controlled-army-supply-transfer.md, supplyTransfer.* in this corpus) — 481 + 1 = 482, one ton past the truncated 481 the general formula alone would give. Corrects the previous round's [derived] reconciliation, which cited docs/design-audit.md Q9 as establishing the free own-city case as a different, TArmyToArmy-shaped dialog from the paid TAFSupply purchase; Q9 itself (docs/design-audit.md:252) lists that exact question as still open, and decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md's own §'Supply is bought, not moved' names the free resupply dialog TAFSupply, the same dialog the cap comes from — so that reconciliation's premise was unsupported by either source it cited, not merely under-evidenced. T38 (docs/task-catalogue.md Done-when 2) moved this field ahead of _provenance and dropped its default, so an omitting ruleset now fails SchemaValidator instead of silently defaulting to 1.
_provenance.autoResupplyPurseTopUpThreshold: derived: supply-capacity-rounding.md — FUN_0044F6D8 (lines 53091-53104), automatic resupply's own-city path: after the free ton transfer, a purse under 500 with a positive treasury gains a flat grant from the treasury. Review round 1, B2: retagged from confirmed — the report's own section heading for this rule is '[derived, then confirmed below]', and the 'confirmed below' paragraph confirms only the troops div 100 cap against 75 save states, not the purse rule; docs/game-design.md:100 already tags it 'confirmed caps; derived purse rule'.
_provenance.autoResupplyPurseTopUpAmount: derived: supply-capacity-rounding.md — the same lines: the flat amount granted is 500, taken from the treasury, not invented money; the report notes this 'fits the many AI armies seen holding exactly 500 or 1,000 money', which is a consistency observation, not a confirmation. The mirror case (purse over 1,000 sends the excess to the treasury) reuses purseCapPerUnit rather than a new field. Review round 1, B2: retagged from confirmed, same reasoning as autoResupplyPurseTopUpThreshold.
_provenance.supplyPercentNumerator: confirmed: decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md — TInformation_ShowArmyDetails prints the supply percentage as supplies × 10000 / troops.
_provenance.mercenaryDesertionSupplyDivisor: confirmed: upkeep-payment-and-desertion.md — a deserting mercenary unit takes troops div 100 tons of the army's supplies with it, equal to the deserting unit's own share of the army's supply capacity. Numerically the same 100 as armySupplyTonsPerTroops but a distinct field: this is the loss-on-desertion divisor, not the capacity formula, the same reasoning already given for populationGrowthMobilizationDivisor.
_provenance.debtWealthDivisor: confirmed: upkeep-payment-and-desertion.md — inDebt = treasury < -(wealth div 500) or treasury < -20000 or unity < 400; wealth is Σ population × 3000, so this line is 6 × total population, capped at 20,000.
_provenance.debtTreasuryFloor: confirmed: upkeep-payment-and-desertion.md — the same debt test's flat -20,000 floor.
_provenance.debtUnityThreshold: confirmed: upkeep-payment-and-desertion.md — the same debt test's unity-under-400 clause.
_provenance.depositionRandomDivisor: confirmed: upkeep-payment-and-desertion.md — an in-debt AI nation has a 1-in-9 chance each quarter of deposing its leader (FUN_0044c8f0), checked in 2 of 15 at-risk nation-quarters, 0 outside the condition.
_provenance.depositionUnityGainAmount: confirmed: upkeep-payment-and-desertion.md — FUN_0044c8f0's unity = max(unity, min(550, unity + 150)); the Gaul deposition (unity 470 -> 550) confirms both this and depositionUnityCeiling exactly.
_provenance.depositionUnityCeiling: confirmed: upkeep-payment-and-desertion.md — the same expression's min(550, ...) ceiling.
_provenance.depositionTreasuryCredit: confirmed: upkeep-payment-and-desertion.md — FUN_0044c8f0's treasury = (treasury < 0) ? 0 : treasury + 1000; the Gaul deposition (treasury -5,030 -> 0) confirms the zero-floor half exactly, and the report notes a positive-treasury nation would gain the flat 1,000.
_provenance.depositionRelationResetThreshold: derived: upkeep-payment-and-desertion.md — FUN_0044c8f0 resets any relation from -5 to -1 (inclusive) with any other nation to 0; code-only, not observed in either sampled deposition (neither deposed nation held such a relation).
_provenance.taxBaseContributionMultiplier: confirmed: nation-tax-base-and-city-economy-fields.md — the quarterly rebuild's cityContribution(city) << 2 (tribute × population / maxPopulation, ×4), and the same ×4 applied by the city-ownership-transfer adjustment (FUN_0044bb18) at capture time.
_provenance.wealthPerPopulationThousand: confirmed: nation-tax-base-and-city-economy-fields.md — nation +0x430 (wealth) += city.population × 3000 every quarter, and ± the same amount at a city-ownership transfer; corrects decompiled-quarterly-billing-and-economy.md and decompiled-city-capture-resolution.md, both of which had this keyed to fortification.
_provenance.treasuryCreditTaxBaseQuarterShareDivisor: confirmed: nation-tax-base-and-city-economy-fields.md — the quarterly treasury credit's second term is taxBase / 4, not mobilization / 4 as decompiled-quarterly-billing-and-economy.md originally read it.
_provenance.treasuryCreditPerCityUpkeep: confirmed: nation-tax-base-and-city-economy-fields.md — treasury -= cityCount (+0x446) × 7 every quarter; the ×7 is per city, not a flat term.
_provenance.tradeIncomeTaxBaseDivisor: confirmed: upkeep-payment-and-desertion.md — FUN_004499ec(n) = Σ over nations j with relation 1 (trade) or 2 (alliance) of taxBase[j] div 12, read from the just-rebuilt tax bases; the human nation's whole-quarter treasury change matched exactly in 6 of 6 quarter pairs once this term was included.
_provenance.populationGrowthGapDivisor: confirmed: city-population-growth.md — d = (maxPop - pop) >> 2, i.e. the gap divided by 4 and truncated; the same 497-city sample fits gap/3 in 366 cases and gap/5 in 398, so /4 is the one uniquely pinned across the full sample.
_provenance.populationGrowthTaxDivisor: confirmed: city-population-growth.md — d' = d - (d × taxRate) / 120 (0x78); pinned together with the mobilization divisor by the one city (Laranda) where both terms bite, and isolated further by the tax17-vs-tax18 controlled-save recipe the report proposes.
_provenance.populationGrowthMobilizationDivisor: confirmed: city-population-growth.md — growth = d' - (d' × mobilized) / 300 + 1; pinned together with the tax divisor by Laranda, the only sampled city where either term changes the predicted growth.
_provenance.populationGrowthConstantAddend: confirmed: city-population-growth.md — the quarterly growth step's trailing +1; dropping it fits only 1 of 497 sampled cities, against 493 with it present.
_provenance.threatenedCityAdjacencyRadius: confirmed: city-population-growth.md — FUN_004497cc checks the 9 cells (a 3×3 block, radius 1) centred on the city for a hostile army; 3 of 3 non-growing, below-maximum cities in the sample had exactly such an army adjacent.
_provenance.unityFloor: confirmed: city-population-growth.md — unity = min(990, max(300, unity + 25 - tax/2 - mobilized/5)); the floor side of the same clamp unityCap's cap side already carries. Matched exactly in 60 of 80 sampled nation-quarters, the other 20 having a battle, capture or elimination event in the round.
_provenance.unityBaseGainPerQuarter: confirmed: city-population-growth.md — unity drifts up by +25 a quarter before the tax/mobilization reductions, correcting decompiled-quarterly-billing-and-economy.md's 'unity decays by 3', which was mobilization's field (see mobilizationDecayPerQuarter).
_provenance.unityTaxRateDivisor: confirmed: city-population-growth.md — the unity update's -taxRate/2 term.
_provenance.unityMobilizationDivisor: confirmed: city-population-growth.md — the unity update's -mobilized/5 term, reading mobilization after this same quarter's decay.
_provenance.lowTaxLoyaltyThresholdPercent: confirmed: decompiled-quarterly-billing-and-economy.md, read by T35 for the first time per city-population-growth.md's transcription of the same FUN_00451b40 city loop — if a nation's tax rate is under 11% and a city's loyalty is below 80, there's a chance loyalty rises.
_provenance.lowTaxLoyaltyCityThreshold: confirmed: decompiled-quarterly-billing-and-economy.md, read by T35 for the first time per city-population-growth.md — the city-loyalty side of the same condition.
_provenance.rebellionLoyaltyThreshold: derived: city-population-growth.md — 'if loyalty < 30 and the city is no nation's capital: FUN_0044c204(city)' [rebellion], transcribed directly from the decompiled quarterly tick rather than save-checked (the rebellion's own choice of new owner depends on an unidentified bitmask and stays open, T17's). Read by T35 for the first time; T08 shipped this field as data nothing read. Supersedes decompiled-quarterly-billing-and-economy.md's earlier, save-unconfirmed 'cities with loyalty under 30 can trigger it' as the citation for the same threshold.
_provenance.loyaltyRiseRollBound: derived: city-population-growth.md — 'loyalty += Random(4)' (0..3), read directly from the code, not save-checked.
_provenance.loyaltyFallProbabilityDenominator: derived: city-population-growth.md — 'if Random(3) == 0', a 1-in-3 roll, read directly from the code, not save-checked.
_provenance.loyaltyFallTaxDivisor: derived: city-population-growth.md — 'loyalty -= Random(taxRate) / 8', read directly from the code, not save-checked.
_provenance.citySupplyBaselineSeasonValue: confirmed: city-population-growth.md §'The weekly step is city supply production' — s = (pop * (v - 40)) / 10; the 40 baseline read against the same season table (supplyConsumption.seasonValues) T08's army consumption already reads. Verified turn-for-turn against a pop-50 city's +50/+200/+200/-100 change across Spring/Summer/Autumn/Winter at mobilization 0.
_provenance.citySupplyProductionDivisor: confirmed: city-population-growth.md, same section — the /10 divisor of the same expression.
_provenance.citySupplyMobilizationDivisor: confirmed: city-population-growth.md, same section — inc = s - (s * mobilized) / 200; mobilization shrinks gains and losses alike. Numerically the same shape as populationGrowthMobilizationDivisor but a distinct field (there 300, here 200; the two formulas are conceptually separate, the same reasoning already given for populationGrowthMobilizationDivisor itself). Verified against Numidia/Illyria/Dacia/Armenia (mob 0, no reduction), Gaul/Celtiberia/Galatia (mob 97-100, exactly half), and Rome (mob 30, 15% less).
_provenance.citySupplyCapTonsPerPopulationThousand: confirmed: city-population-growth.md, same section — supplies = max(0, min(supplies + inc, pop * 10)); Rome's capital (pop 181) holds exactly 1,810 in several saves.
_provenance.famineLoyaltyLossProbabilityDenominator: confirmed: city-population-growth.md §'Weekly supply: 33 pairs' — 'Winter famine: loyalty, 1 in 3. In Winter pairs, cities whose stock ends the turn at 0 lost exactly 1 loyalty in 39 of 108 cases (36%; 1/3 expected) and kept it in 69.' Numerically the same 3 as loyaltyFallProbabilityDenominator but a distinct field: this is the weekly, Winter-only, empty-stock roll, not T35's quarterly, tax-rate-gated one.
_provenance.famineLoyaltyLossAmount: confirmed: city-population-growth.md, same section — the flat 1-point loyalty loss on that roll; 'cities with stock left, and every city outside Winter, never lose loyalty this way (1,874 and 8,980 city-turns unchanged, apart from a handful of other events)'.

_provenance.troopsPerCostUnit: confirmed: decompiled-recruitment-cost-formula.md — cost = (troops / 200) × priceTable[unitType], the same table for initial recruitment and quarterly upkeep.
_provenance.mercenaryPoolSlots: confirmed: decompiled-sav-file-layout.md — the mercenary table is exactly 50 slots of 12 bytes, hard-coded in the save/load code (mercenary-pool-record.md had found the same figure empirically).
_provenance.mercenaryHireTroopDivisor: confirmed: decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md — hire cost = (troops × quarterlyPrice[type]) / 1000 × quality, paid from the hiring army's own purse.
_provenance.mercenaryUpkeepQualityDivisor: confirmed: decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md — mercenary upkeep is ((troops / 200) × price[type] × quality) / 5 against a regular's (troops / 200) × price[type].

_provenance.maxUnitsPerArmy: confirmed: decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md — TUnitMap_JoinArmies caps the combined army at 20 units.
_provenance.maxTroopsPerArmy: confirmed: decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md — and the same 100,000 cap is enforced on mercenary hire.
_provenance.maxArmies: confirmed: decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md — FUN_00449F08 refuses to create an army once 198 exist (< 0xC6).
_provenance.splitMinUnits: confirmed: decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md — TUnitMap_SplitArmy needs at least 2 units.
_provenance.newArmyMorale: confirmed: decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md — a freshly split army is created with morale 0x3B = 59.
_provenance.newArmyMovesHumanSeat: confirmed: decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md — 0 moves for a human nation.
_provenance.newArmyMovesAiSeat: confirmed: decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md — 1 move for an AI one. This is one of the seat asymmetries the flags block selects between.

_provenance.buildCostPerShip: confirmed: fleet-order-at-caere.md and decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md — a fleet order costs ships × 10 talents.
_provenance.orderMinShips: confirmed: decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md — TBuildFleet_ChangeFleetSize clamps an order to 10..100 ships.
_provenance.constructionTicks: confirmed: decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md — the construction counter starts at 24 and decrements weekly; the Caere order's 12-ticks-to-go reading twelve weeks later confirms it in save data.
_provenance.launchConditionPercent: confirmed: decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md — FUN_0044A050 sets fleet +20 to 100 on launch.
_provenance.transportTroopsPerShip: confirmed: decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md — the embark check refuses when ships < troops / 500.
_provenance.repairCostDivisor: confirmed: decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md — repair costs ships × points / 5 talents and zeroes the fleet's moves.
_provenance.joinMaxShips: confirmed: decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md — TUnitMap_JoinFleets refuses a combined fleet above 100 ships.
_provenance.splitMinShips: confirmed: decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md — TUnitMap_SplitFleet needs at least 20 ships.
_provenance.maxConditionPercent: confirmed: decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md — TRepairFleet clamps a repair order to 0..(100 - condition).
_provenance.stormDamageRandomDivisor: confirmed: supply-driven-morale-and-fleet-attrition.md / investigations/thracia-supply-morale.md — dmg = max(1, random(100 - condition) / 10), the storm pass's base roll, unconditional and not supply-driven.
_provenance.stormWinterDamageMultiplier: confirmed: same reports — if (season == winter) dmg = min(5, dmg * 2).
_provenance.stormWinterDamageCap: confirmed: same reports — the cap of the Winter doubling.
_provenance.stormTripleDamageMultiplier: confirmed: same reports — if (fleet[+24] == 1) dmg = min(8, dmg * 3).

_provenance.cityPopulationTierThresholds: OMITTED (ships empty) — and here is exactly what was searched and exactly what was found, because an earlier revision of this note claimed the search came up empty when it had not. What the reports DO establish: rivers-and-map-markers.md ('City and unit overlays') finds that all 334 city cells satisfy 'map code = 20 + owner code + 16 × variant' with variants 0-4, holding for 334/334 cities in the checked save — so a five-value display axis on city markers is well evidenced, the direct counterpart of the three army bands and three fleet bands in decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md part 3. What the reports do NOT establish: that same sentence says the variant's meaning — 'city size, icon, or another display category' — still needs confirmation, and the report's own next-check item 3 is 'confirm the city-marker variant meanings'. There is no decompiled banding function for cities analogous to FUN_0044A80C/FUN_0044A878, so no population boundary is recorded anywhere. Shipping 5 as a size-tier count would assert the unconfirmed half (that the variant means size); shipping any threshold would invent a number outright. So this ships empty and docs/game-design.md §'City and army markers scale with size' is left standing as a requirement rather than a spec. Closing it needs that report's next-check item 3, after which the thresholds arrive as data with no model change.
